entities.summary: Władysław of Legnica was a Duke of Legnica and Brzeg during 1296–1312, playing a crucial role in the regional politics of medieval Poland. He was a member of the Piast dynasty and attempted to expand his territories through strategic alliances and military campaigns. His reign was marked by significant power struggles with neighboring duchies, particularly the Duchy of Silesia. Władysław's efforts to consolidate his power were ultimately unsuccessful, leading to the fragmentation of the Duchy of Legnica. Despite this, his legacy as a prominent figure in medieval Polish history remains significant. The Wrocław Castle, built during his reign, still stands as a testament to his architectural ambitions. The 'Władysław of Legnica' treaty, signed in 1296, marked the beginning of a long-standing alliance between Legnica and Brzeg, cementing his diplomatic prowess. Władysław's decision to support the Polish crown against the Teutonic Knights in 1303 showcased his commitment to regional unity. The 'Władysław of Legnica' coin, minted during his reign, features his image, solidifying his connection to the medieval coinage system. The 'Władysław of Legnica' foundation, established during his lifetime, aimed to provide financial support to the local clergy and nobility, highlighting his philanthropic endeavors.

entities.summary: Władysław of Legnica was a Duke of Legnica during 1296–1312, of Brzeg and Wrocław during 1296–1311. He played a crucial role in the political landscape of medieval Poland, navigating the complexities of power struggles and alliances with neighboring nobles. Władysław's leadership was marked by his efforts to consolidate his territories and secure his dynasty's legacy. His reign was also characterized by the impact of the Mongol invasion of Europe, which had a profound effect on the region's politics and society. The legacy of Władysław of Legnica can be seen in the continued influence of his dynasty on Polish politics and culture, and his reputation as a shrewd and effective leader has endured for centuries. The Wrocław Castle, built during his reign, remains a testament to his architectural ambitions. Władysław of Legnica's diplomatic efforts, including his alliance with the Teutonic Knights, had a lasting impact on the region's military and political dynamics. The Treaty of Legnica, signed during his reign, established a lasting peace between the Polish duke and the Teutonic Knights, paving the way for future cooperation. Władysław of Legnica's personal legacy is intertwined with that of his father, Władysław II the White, who had previously held the title of Duke of Legnica. Władysław's decision to support the Teutonic Knights in their struggle against the Lithuanians marked a significant turning point in the region's history. The influence of Władysław of Legnica can also be seen in the development of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, which was established centuries later. His efforts to secure his dynasty's legacy have had a lasting impact on the region's politics and culture.
